literal_source_claim_zh: 随机微分方程的动力学
statement_blocker: The repository supplies only a subject label and broad gloss. It does not select a stochastic or random differential equation, base metric dynamical system, time and state spaces, solution and cocycle conventions, local/global scope, hypotheses, or a theorem conclusion. Arnold's 1998 monograph contains multiple inequivalent candidate definitions and theorems, so choosing one would substitute missing mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: an exact source must fix the probability/noise base and base action, time monoid or group, measurable/topological/smooth state space and universes, stochastic driver and filtration where applicable, and all regularity, completeness, compactness, and separability assumptions.
conclusion: Open: the source supplies no truth-valued conclusion selecting cocycle construction or perfection, SDE-to-RDS generation or converse representation, continuity or smoothness, invariant measure, stability, or another dynamical property.
excluded_degenerate_cases: None are frozen at intake because no proposition has been selected. The statement phase must resolve every case listed in degenerate_cases_to_resolve from the accepted source.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Arnold monograph Section 1.1 definition and basic properties of a random dynamical system or cocycle
Arnold monograph Theorem 1.3.2 perfection of a crude cocycle and its corollaries
Arnold monograph Theorems 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 that local/global random differential equations generate absolutely-continuous-in-time random dynamical systems
Arnold monograph Theorem 2.2.13 converse representation for absolutely-continuous-in-time random dynamical systems
Arnold monograph Theorems 2.3.26 and 2.3.29 for global/local semimartingale-driven stochastic differential equations generating semimartingale random dynamical systems
Arnold monograph Theorem 2.3.30 converse semimartingale representation
a source-specified existence, invariant-measure, regularity, stability, or long-time theorem
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: trivial probability or state spaces and deterministic zero-noise systems
zero time, one-sided time, and absence of inverse base shifts
global solutions versus local solutions with finite explosion time
nonunique weak or strong solutions and dependence on chosen versions
null exceptional sets depending on time, noise, or initial state
pathwise equality, indistinguishability, and almost-sure equality conventions
perfect cocycle identities versus crude identities holding separately almost surely
separate versus joint measurability and continuous versus smooth state dependence
excluded_substitutions: a definition of a filtration, adapted process, Markov kernel, measure-preserving map, or deterministic flow
a deterministic ODE flow, finite stochastic simulation, numerical sample path, or generic Markov-chain theorem
a structure that assumes the desired cocycle, solution, invariant measure, or conclusion as data
